samples.label: A20. Deaths in home fires by sex, age group, house type, region, month and year
samples.source: Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency
note:
Statistics on deaths within 30 days of a fire due to burns or smoke inhalation, as assessed by the Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency on the basis of information from the municipal fire and rescue service, the police, the Swedish Transport Administration, the National Forensic Centre (1999-2015) and the national burns centres in Linköping and Uppsala.

It can take more than a year for the Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency to receive information on fire deaths. This table is based on the latest assessments made by the Agency, and the most recent figures may be subject to revision as more data is provided.

In these statistics, a residential building is understood to be either a block of flats, a detached house, a terraced or semi-detached house or a summer house. 

Institutional forms of accommodation such as sheltered housing, care homes, nursing homes, communal housing and student residences are not included in this category.

kommunkod.label: region
note: Statistics at the municipal level must be interpreted with care. Fatal fires are infrequent events even in the largest municipalities, and random variation has a relatively large influence on the outcome for any particular year. The Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency receives many requests for municipal data and has decided to publish the figures even though it is difficult to draw reliable conclusions from statistics at the municipal level.
